question: Does Dual-Stream Attentive Readout (DSAR) combined with Pair Update LayerNorm improve upon the GPTrans-T 100K baseline (0.156627 eV) under the frozen 100K contract without auxiliary node denoising?

hypothesis.observed_deficiency: Standard GPTrans-T discards all 7,680 dimensions of real atomic representations produced across 12 layers, relying solely on a single 256-dim virtual node. In quantum chemistry, HOMO-LUMO Gap is a collective orbital property strongly dependent on local chromophores and conjugated systems. DSAR adaptively pools real atomic features alongside the virtual token.
alternative_explanations: The virtual token already captures all necessary orbital density through 12 layers of self-attention
Concatenating pooled atom features increases readout overfitting on the 100K training subset
hypothesis.changed_mechanism: Dual-Stream Attentive Readout combining [CLS] virtual token, virtual self-loop pair, and learnable attentive atom pooling over all non-padding nodes with Pair Update LayerNorm into an expanded 544-dim readout head
hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: 60-epoch 100K/50K run failing to achieve 0.003 eV gain over the 0.156627 eV baseline (threshold < 0.153627 eV)
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: nominate Dual-Stream Attentive Readout (DSAR) as the new standard readout layer across all GPTrans variants
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: retain single virtual-token readout and close attentive atom pooling
